content_rewards_fee.verified: Content Rewards' own articles/pricing: 10% platform fee on each payout (8% for verified organisations), charged only on delivered work, taken as each approved clip settles; minimum campaign budget $1,000.
conflicts: Whether the 10% comes off the creator's payout or is added on the brand side is described both ways in summaries (articles: 'brands pay', other guides: 'creator fee on CPM campaigns'). Treat the creator's take as possibly rate x 0.9 until confirmed on the live payout screen.

Older Content Rewards FAQ pages cite 7% (looks outdated); a ClipSpeed guide says per-post/retainer campaigns pay 10% below a $5,000 budget and 0% at $5,000+ (unverified); FindClout says Whop does not publish the fee on brand-facing pages.

verified: Brand sets a per-video minimum payout; a video below it never reaches review (Whop docs example: $3/1K rate with $6 minimum = only videos with ~2,000 views get reviewed).
The brand/campaign team approves clips, not Content Rewards; no fixed review time.
CPM campaigns pay in rounds: 7 days of earning + 3-day hold, about every 10 days.
For clips submitted since 25 Sep 2026, CPM earning stops 30 days after submission.

Pool campaigns: allocated when the pool ends, split by your approved counted views / qualifying total; a creator must meet the pool's minimum across approved submissions; minimum cannot change after launch; shown estimates are not guaranteed; 3-day hold; CR may end a pool after 30 days without new approved submissions; if nobody qualifies, funds stay with the campaign.
Paused campaign (budget spent): approved clips keep paying, new views stop earning until topped up.
Withdrawals from $1; moving Content Rewards earnings to the Whop balance is free; standard payout to bank/PayPal/wallet up to 5 business days; instant payouts carry a Whop fee (amount not stated).

earnings_evidence.not_found: No independent or audited data on what clippers actually net per 1K views after fees, rejections and caps. Guides (FindClout, OpenClip) say real net is almost always below the listed rate and advise dividing paid dollars by paid views over two weeks.
estimates_labelled: ESTIMATE: at a $1.00/1K listed rate, net is ~$0.90/1K if the 10% fee comes off the creator side; effective rate is lower once sub-minimum clips, rejected clips and views beyond the per-clip cap are counted.
ESTIMATE: Lacy pool implied rate across all views so far = $12,500 / ~60.7M views = ~$0.21/1K, paid only to creators above 1M approved views.
ESTIMATE: Kai Cenat pool = $10,000 / ~6.7M views = ~$1.49/1K at the Nov 20 snapshot, falling as views grow; only creators above 750K approved views share.

ESTIMATE: Clix pool had only ~399K total views on Nov 18 across 149 creators; if the 400K bar is per creator (as the pool article describes minimums), few or none had qualified then, so a creator who clears 400K could take a large share. High variance.

Lacy minimum conflict: brief said 750K total approved views; two Content Rewards articles say 1,000,000 approved views per creator for Lacy, and 750K for Kai Cenat. Treat 1M as the current published figure until the rules page is read.

Pools vs per-view: GTA 6 pools (Lacy $12.5K/1M, Kai Cenat $10K/750K, YourRAGE $5K/500K, Clix $5K/400K) pay nothing below the per-creator minimum. For a new small channel, per-view campaigns with low per-clip minimums are the realistic option.
